prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

Labour Party Manifesto 2005 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core vision
- “Forward, not back”: government’s duty is to provide opportunity and security for all, pairing economic dynamism with social justice, and matching rights with responsibilities.
- Embed a new progressive consensus: stable economy, world-class public services, safer communities, global engagement.

Record since 1997
- Economy: longest period of uninterrupted growth; lowest sustained inflation/interest rates for a generation; 2 million more in work; 300,000 more businesses; poverty reduced among children and pensioners.
- Public services: big rises in education and NHS investment; more teachers/nurses; heart and cancer deaths down; free entry boosts museum visits.
- Communities: crime down ~30%; more police and Community Support Officers; faster justice for persistent young offenders.
- Global: influence in enlarged EU; aid more than doubled; UK led on emissions trading.

Economy and enterprise
- Maintain low inflation (2% target), prudent debt, and fiscal rules; no rise in basic or top income tax; protect zero VAT items.
- Goal of full employment (80% employment rate); raise minimum wage; welfare-to-work and Incapacity Benefit reform with support and obligations.
- Back business: competitive taxes (low corporation/capital gains), R&D credits, drive efficiency in regulation; promote skills, apprenticeships, and a 10‑year science strategy (lift R&D to 2.5% of GDP by 2014).
- Energy and infrastructure: mixed energy strategy (renewables, nuclear, clean coal, microgeneration); £180bn+ public transport investment to 2015; consider national road pricing; expand rail capacity (high-speed options), buses, and safety.

Education and skills
- Personalised learning; higher standards in basics; stronger in-service training; parental engagement and school discipline.
- Every secondary an independent specialist school; expand Academies (200 by 2010); modern school buildings (Building Schools for the Future).
- Strengthen vocational routes: specialised diplomas, more apprenticeships; Education Maintenance Allowances.
- Higher education: increase participation toward 50% by 2010; variable fees capped at £3,000 with grants/bursaries for poorer students; boost research.

Crime, security, migration
- Neighbourhood policing teams in every community by 2010; more CSOs; single non-emergency number.
- Tough on antisocial behaviour (ASBOs, Alcohol Disorder Zones), youth interventions, drug testing/treatment expansion.
- Serious Organised Crime Agency; tighter gun/knife laws; manage reoffending with offender management, tagging; seize criminal assets.
- Immigration: points-based system favouring skills; English tests for settlement; employer penalties for illegal working; biometric visas/ePassports; phased ID cards. Faster, firmer asylum processes. New counter‑terror powers alongside prosecution.

Health and healthy living
- NHS investment to triple by 2008; more staff, capacity, and community hospitals; maximum 18 weeks from referral to treatment by 2008; patient choice of hospital; use independent sector to add capacity; stronger hygiene and governance; dentistry review.
- Public health: better school meals and food standards, simple nutrition labelling, expanded stop-smoking services; largely smoke‑free enclosed workplaces.

Older people
- Pension Credit lifts minimum incomes; Winter Fuel Payments; free off‑peak bus travel. Seek cross‑party pensions settlement post‑Pensions Commission; flexible retirement and personal budgets in care.

Families, childcare, housing
- Halve child poverty by 2010–11; expand tax credits and Child Trust Fund.
- Universal Sure Start Children’s Centres; free nursery hours rising; extended schools offering childcare 8am–6pm to age 14; longer paid maternity leave (to 9 months, aiming 12); extend flexible working rights.
- Boost home ownership (shared ownership, stamp duty threshold rise); increase and improve social housing; choice‑based lettings.

International, environment, culture, democracy
- Europe: lead reform; support Constitutional Treaty; euro only if tests met. Defence: modernise forces; retain nuclear deterrent. Support democracy in Iraq/Afghanistan; revitalize Middle East peace efforts.
- Climate and development: meet/extend Kyoto aims (20% CO2 cut by 2010; 60% by 2050); lead on G8 Africa agenda, aid to 0.7% GNI by 2013, debt relief, fairer trade rules.
- Culture/sport: free national museums; widen participation; invest in facilities and school sport; Olympic bid/legacy; digital switchover 2008–2012; BBC governance reform.
- Democracy: deepen devolution; empower neighbourhoods and councils; reform House of Lords (remove remaining hereditaries; free vote on composition); strengthen equality and human rights (Single Equality Act; new Commission).
